title: Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants
syllabus: Flower structure; Development of male and female gametophytes; Pollination - types, agencies and examples; Outbreeding devices; Pollen-Pistil interaction; Double fertilization; Post-fertilization events - Development of endosperm and embryo, Development of seed and formation of fruit; Special modes - Apomixis, parthenocarpy, polyembryony; Significance of seed and fruit formation.

questions.question: The innermost layer of the microsporangial wall, which nourishes the developing pollen grains and possesses dense cytoplasm with more than one nucleus, is the:
questions.solution: The microsporangium is surrounded by four wall layers: epidermis, endothecium, middle layers, and the tapetum. The tapetum is the innermost layer that nourishes developing microspores/pollen grains; its cells possess dense cytoplasm and are generally multinucleate.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the microsporangial wall layers and their respective structural features:

List-I (Wall Layer)List-II (Structural / Functional Feature)
(A) Epidermis(I) Outermost protective single layer of cells
(B) Endothecium(II) Possesses fibrous alpha-cellulosic bands; aids in dehiscence
(C) Middle layers(III) 1 to 3 short-lived parenchymatous layers
(D) Tapetum(IV) Secretes sporopollenin, callase, and nourishes microspores

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: The epidermis is the outermost protective layer; the endothecium develops hygroscopic fibrous bands aiding anther dehiscence; the middle layers are 1-3 ephemeral layers; the tapetum nourishes microspores and synthesizes sporopollenin precursors and pollenkit.

questions.question: Sporopollenin, which forms the outer exine layer of pollen grains, is recognized as one of the most resistant biological materials because:
options: It can withstand high temperatures, strong acids, and alkalis, and no enzyme that degrades it is known
It is a water-soluble carbohydrate that binds readily to water
It is digested easily by pectinases during pollen germination
It is composed entirely of cellulose and hemicellulose
questions.solution: Sporopollenin is an oxidative polymer of carotenoids and fatty acid esters forming the pollen exine. It can withstand high temperatures, strong acids, and alkali, and no biological enzyme is known to degrade sporopollenin, which allows pollen grains to be preserved as fossils.

questions.question: In over 60 percent of angiosperms, pollen grains are shed at which developmental stage?
options: 2-celled stage (one vegetative cell and one generative cell)
3-celled stage (one vegetative cell and two male gametes)
questions.solution: In over 60 per cent of angiosperms, pollen grains are shed at the 2-celled stage (a larger vegetative cell and a smaller generative cell). In the remaining species, the generative cell divides mitotically to give rise to two male gametes before pollen grains are shed (3-celled stage).

questions.question: The vegetative cell of a mature pollen grain differs from the generative cell because the vegetative cell:
options: Is bigger, has abundant food reserve, and has a large irregularly shaped nucleus
Is small, spindle-shaped with dense cytoplasm, and floats in the generative cell
Divides mitotically to form two male gametes
Lacks an intine and contains sporopollenin
questions.solution: The vegetative cell is bigger, contains abundant reserve food materials, and has a large irregularly shaped nucleus. The generative cell is small, spindle-shaped with dense cytoplasm and a distinct nucleus, and floats in the cytoplasm of the vegetative cell.

questions.question: Parthenium or carrot grass, which entered India as a contaminant with imported wheat, is notorious for causing:
options: Pollen allergies and chronic respiratory disorders like asthma and bronchitis
Severe root gall disease in crops
Immediate loss of seed viability in legumes
questions.solution: Parthenium hysterophorus (carrot grass) came into India as a contaminant with imported wheat and has become ubiquitous in occurrence, causing severe pollen allergies, allergic rhinitis, asthma, and skin dermatitis.

questions.question: In which of the following families of angiosperms do pollen grains retain viability for several months?
questions.solution: In some cereals such as rice and wheat, pollen grains lose viability within 30 minutes of their release. In some members of Rosaceae, Leguminosae, and Solanaceae, pollen grains maintain viability for several months.

questions.question: Pollen grains of a large number of species can be stored for years in liquid nitrogen at which temperature for crop breeding programmes?
questions.solution: Pollen grains can be stored for years in liquid nitrogen at $-196^\circ\text{C}$ (cryopreservation). Such stored pollen can be used as pollen banks, similar to seed banks, in crop breeding programmes.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the parts of a typical anatropous ovule (Megasporangium):

List-I (Ovular Structure)List-II (Anatomical Description)
(A) Funicle(I) Stalk by which the ovule is attached to the placenta
(B) Hilum(II) Junction region where the body of ovule fuses with the funicle
(C) Micropyle(III) Small pore at the apex where integuments do not cover the nucellus
(D) Chalaza(IV) Basal part of the ovule opposite the micropylar end

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Funicle: Stalk attaching ovule to placenta; Hilum: Scar/junction where funicle fuses with ovule body; Micropyle: Small terminal pore left by integuments; Chalaza: Basal swollen region representing the base of the ovule.

questions.question: A typical mature female gametophyte (embryo sac) in most angiosperms (Polygonum type) is derived monosporically and consists of:
questions.solution: A typical Polygonum-type embryo sac develops from a single functional megaspore through three sequential free-nuclear mitotic divisions, resulting in an 8-nucleate, 7-celled organization at maturity (3 antipodals, 1 central cell with 2 polar nuclei, 2 synergids, and 1 egg cell).

questions.question: The filiform apparatus is a specialized cellular thickening present at the micropylar tip of the:
questions.solution: The synergids have special cellular finger-like thickenings at their micropylar tip called the filiform apparatus, which plays a critical role in guiding the pollen tube into the synergid.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the cellular composition of a mature Angiosperm Embryo Sac:

List-I (Embryo Sac Region)List-II (Constituent Cells / Nuclei)
(A) Egg apparatus(I) 3 cells located at the chalazal end
(B) Central cell(II) 2 synergids and 1 egg cell at the micropylar end
(C) Antipodals(III) Largest binucleate cell containing two polar nuclei

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Egg apparatus (micropylar end): 2 synergids + 1 egg cell; Central cell: Single large central cell with 2 polar nuclei; Antipodals (chalazal end): 3 cells that degenerate after fertilization.

questions.question: Cleistogamous flowers are bisexual flowers that do not open at all. Which of the following statements is INCORRECT regarding cleistogamy?
options: Cleistogamous flowers show extensive outcrossing and high genetic diversity.
They ensure seed-set even in the complete absence of pollinators.
questions.solution: Cleistogamous flowers never open; anthers and stigma lie close to each other, ensuring 100% autogamy and guaranteed seed set without pollinators. However, this eliminates outcrossing and cross-pollination, leading to inbreeding and reduced genetic variability.

questions.question: Geitonogamy refers to the transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma of another flower of the same plant. Functionally and genetically it is categorized as:
options: Functionally cross-pollination (involving a pollinating agent), but genetically similar to autogamy
questions.solution: Geitonogamy is functionally cross-pollination because it involves an external pollinating agent, but genetically it is equivalent to autogamy since all pollen grains originate from the same genetic parent.

questions.question: Which of the following modes of pollination is the ONLY type that brings genetically different types of pollen grains to the stigma during pollination?
questions.solution: Xenogamy is the transfer of pollen grains from anther to the stigma of a flower on a different plant of the same species. This is the only type of pollination which brings genetically diverse pollen grains to the stigma.

questions.question: Wind-pollinated (anemophilous) flowers typically possess which of the following sets of adaptations?
options: Light and non-sticky pollen grains, well-exposed stamens, feathery stigma, and a single ovule in each ovary
Sticky, heavy pollen grains, brightly colored petals, and nectar guides
Pollen grains surrounded by a sticky mucilage covering and no stigmas
Flowers with intense fragrances and large clusters of nectar glands
questions.solution: Wind-pollinated flowers have light and non-sticky pollen grains, well-exposed stamens to facilitate wind dispersal, large feathery stigmas to easily trap airborne pollen, small inconspicuous non-scented flowers, and often a single ovule in each ovary arranged in an inflorescence (e.g., corn cob tassels, grasses).

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the types of Hydrophily (water pollination) and plant examples:

List-I (Pollination Mode / Plant)List-II (Pollination Mechanism)
(A) Vallisneria(I) Female flower reaches water surface by long stalk; passive surface pollination (Epihydrophily)
(B) Zostera (Sea grass)(II) Female flowers remain submerged; long ribbon-like pollen grains carried underwater (Hypohydrophily)
(C) Eichhornia (Water hyacinth)(III) Aquatic plant with emergent flowers pollinated by insects or wind

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: In Vallisneria, pollination occurs on the surface of water via long pedicels; in marine sea grasses like Zostera, long ribbon-like pollen grains without exine are carried underwater; in Eichhornia and Nymphaea (water lily), flowers emerge above water and are pollinated by insects or wind.

questions.question: Yucca plant and the moth Pronuba yuccasella exhibit an obligate mutualistic relationship because:
options: The moth deposits its eggs in the locule of the ovary and pollinates the flower, while larvae develop from eggs as seeds mature
The moth feeds entirely on the nectar without pollinating
The plant provides vegetative galls for moth larvae
The moth causes cleistogamy in the flowers
questions.solution: A mutualistic obligate relationship exists between the moth Tegeticula/Pronuba and the Yucca plant: the moth lays its eggs inside the ovarian locule and cross-pollinates the flower. The larvae hatch from the eggs as the seeds begin developing.

questions.question: Which of the following outbreeding devices is a genetically controlled mechanism that prevents self-pollen from fertilizing the ovules by inhibiting pollen germination or pollen tube growth in the pistil?
questions.solution: Self-incompatibility is a genetically controlled pre-zygotic mechanism (often controlled by multiple alleles at an S-locus) that prevents self-pollen (from the same flower or other flowers of the same plant) from fertilising the ovules by inhibiting pollen germination or pollen tube growth in the pistil.

questions.question: In Papaya (Carica papaya), male and female flowers are present on different plants (dioecious condition). This condition completely PREVENTS:
questions.solution: In dioecious plants like papaya, male and female flowers are borne on separate individual plants (dioecy), which prevents both autogamy (self-pollination in same flower) and geitonogamy (pollination between different flowers of the same plant).

questions.question: In artificial hybridization programmes of hermaphrodite crop plants, the removal of anthers from the flower bud before the anther dehisces is called:
questions.solution: If the female parent bears bisexual flowers, removal of anthers from the flower bud before the anther dehisces using a pair of forceps is necessary. This technique is called emasculation.

questions.question: Double fertilization is a unique diagnostic phenomenon of angiosperms discovered by S.G. Nawaschin (1898). It consists of which two fusion events?
options: Syngamy (Generative fertilization) and Triple Fusion (Vegetative fertilization)
Fusion of two polar nuclei with one synergid
Fusion of antipodals with the male gamete
questions.solution: Double fertilization involves: (1) Syngamy: One male gamete ($n$) fuses with the egg cell ($n$) to form a diploid zygote ($2n$), and (2) Triple Fusion: The second male gamete ($n$) fuses with the diploid secondary nucleus ($2n$, formed by two polar nuclei) in the central cell to form the triploid Primary Endosperm Nucleus (PEN, $3n$).

questions.question: The Primary Endosperm Cell (PEC) resulting from triple fusion develops into the endosperm, whose cells have a ploidy level of:
questions.solution: The central cell after triple fusion becomes the Primary Endosperm Cell (PEC) and develops into the nutritive endosperm tissue, which is typically triploid ($3n$) in angiosperms.

questions.question: In tender coconut, the milky coconut water represents ________, while the surrounding white kernel represents ________:
options: Free-nuclear endosperm (thousands of free nuclei), Cellular endosperm
questions.solution: The coconut water from tender coconut is free-nuclear endosperm (made up of thousands of free nuclei), and the surrounding white kernel/meat is the cellular endosperm.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the types of mature seeds based on endosperm presence:

List-I (Seed Category)List-II (Examples)
(A) Non-albuminous (Exalbuminous / Non-endospermic)(I) Castor, Cotton, Maize, Wheat, Barley
(B) Albuminous (Endospermic)(II) Pea, Groundnut, Gram, Beans
(C) Perispermic seeds(III) Black pepper and Beet

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Non-albuminous seeds consume endosperm completely before seed maturation (Pea, Groundnut, Gram, Bean); Albuminous seeds retain endosperm as reserve food (Wheat, Maize, Barley, Castor); Perispermic seeds retain persistent remnants of nucellus called perisperm (Black pepper, Beet).

questions.question: Persistent, residual nucellus observed in seeds of black pepper and beet is called:
questions.solution: In some seeds such as black pepper and beet, remnants of nucellus are persistent and remain unconsumed. This residual, persistent nutritive nucellar tissue is called perisperm.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the structures of an Angiosperm Dicot and Monocot Embryo:

List-I (Embryonic Part)List-II (Anatomical Identity)
(A) Scutellum(I) Undifferentiated protective sheath enclosing the radicle and root cap
(B) Coleoptile(II) Single large shield-shaped lateral cotyledon in grass family
(C) Coleorhiza(III) Hollow foliar sheath enclosing the shoot apex and leaf primordia
(D) Epiblast(IV) Reduced rudimentary remnant of the second cotyledon in grasses

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: In grass embryos: Scutellum = shield-shaped cotyledon; Coleoptile = foliar sheath covering the plumule; Coleorhiza = protective sheath covering the radicle; Epiblast = rudimentary flap representing the second cotyledon.

questions.question: False fruits (pseudocarps) are fruits where other floral parts like the thalamus contribute to fruit formation. Classic examples of false fruits include:
questions.solution: In a few species such as apple, strawberry, and cashew, the thalamus also contributes to fruit formation; such fruits are called false fruits (pseudocarps). Fruits developing exclusively from the ovary are true fruits.

questions.question: Parthenocarpic fruits are fruits that develop WITHOUT fertilization and are seedless. A naturally occurring example is:
questions.solution: Banana is a naturally occurring parthenocarpic fruit developing without fertilization, making it seedless. Parthenocarpy can also be induced artificially through the application of plant growth hormones such as auxins and gibberellins.

questions.question: Apomixis is a special form of reproduction seen in Asteraceae and grasses that is defined as:
options: A form of asexual reproduction that mimics sexual reproduction, producing seeds without fertilization
Formation of seeds with double fertilization
Fusion of two male gametes with a single egg cell
questions.solution: Apomixis is a form of asexual reproduction that mimics sexual reproduction, wherein seeds are formed without fertilization (e.g., in some species of Asteraceae and grasses).

questions.question: In Citrus and Mango varieties, polyembryony (occurrence of more than one embryo in a seed) arises primarily due to:
options: Maternal nucellar cells surrounding the embryo sac dividing, protruding into the embryo sac, and developing into multiple embryos
Multiple pollen tubes entering a single synergid
Cleavage of a single endosperm nucleus
Development of antipodal cells into functional seeds
questions.solution: In many Citrus and Mango varieties, some of the maternal diploid nucellar cells surrounding the embryo sac begin dividing, protrude into the embryo sac, and develop into maternal diploid embryos (adventive polyembryony).

questions.question: Why is the introduction of apomictic genes considered of immense commercial value in hybrid seed production for farmers?
options: It prevents segregation of desirable hybrid traits in the progeny, eliminating the need to purchase costly hybrid seeds every year
It triples the number of cotyledons in each seed
It makes the crops independent of light for photosynthesis
It causes all flowers to become cleistogamous
questions.solution: If hybrids are made into apomicts, there is no segregation of characters in the hybrid progeny. Farmers can then keep using the hybrid seeds to raise new crops year after year without buying expensive hybrid seeds every season.

questions.question:
Read the following statements regarding the viability of seeds:
Statement I: Lupinus arcticus excavated from Arctic Tundra holds the record for germinating and flowering after an estimated 10,000 years of dormancy.
Statement II: A 2,000-year-old viable seed of Date Palm (Phoenix dactylifera) was discovered during archaeological excavation at King Herod’s Palace near the Dead Sea.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.solution: Both statements are correct according to NCERT. Lupinus arcticus holds the record of ~10,000 years of seed viability, while Phoenix dactylifera seeds excavated from King Herod's palace remained viable after ~2,000 years.

questions.question: The micropyle remains as a small pore in the seed coat of a mature seed. Its primary functional significance during seed germination is to:
options: Facilitate the entry of water and oxygen into the seed
Allow the exit of stored endosperm
Enable sunlight to reach the cotyledons
Prevent fungi from infecting the radicle
questions.solution: The micropyle remains as a small pore in the seed coat. This facilitates the entry of water and dissolved oxygen into the seed during imbibition and germination.

questions.question: A dicot embryo typically consists of an embryonal axis and two cotyledons. The portion of the embryonal axis ABOVE the level of cotyledons is the ________, which terminates in the ________:
questions.solution: The portion of embryonal axis above the level of cotyledons is the epicotyl, which terminates with the plumule (embryonic shoot/stem tip). The cylindrical portion below the level of cotyledons is the hypocotyl, which terminates at its lower end in the radicle.

questions.question: In a fertilized ovule, which of the following maternal structures transforms into the tough protective outer seed coat (Testa)?
questions.solution: During seed formation: Outer integument develops into the outer hard seed coat (testa); Inner integument develops into the inner thin seed coat (tegmen); Ovary wall develops into the fruit wall (pericarp).

questions.question: During the post-pollination development on the stigma, the pollen tube discharges its two male gametes into the:
options: Cytoplasm of one of the degenerating synergids
questions.solution: The pollen tube enters one of the synergids through the filiform apparatus and ruptures, releasing the two male gametes into the cytoplasm of the degenerate synergid. One gamete moves to fuse with the egg cell, and the other moves to fuse with the polar nuclei in the central cell.

questions.question: In anther cross-section, the cells of which tissue undergo meiotic divisions to form microspore tetrads during microsporogenesis?
questions.solution: As the anther develops, the cells of the central sporogenous tissue undergo meiotic divisions to form microspore tetrads. Each cell of the sporogenous tissue is capable of giving rise to a microspore tetrad and is a potential pollen mother cell (PMC).

questions.question: The intine (inner wall layer) of a pollen grain is a thin and continuous layer composed of:
questions.solution: The inner wall of the pollen grain is called the intine. It is a thin and continuous non-sculptured layer made up of cellulose and pectin.

questions.question: Germ pores on the pollen grain surface are prominent aperture areas where:
options: Sporopollenin is absent in the exine
Both exine and intine are completely missing
questions.solution: Pollen grain exine has prominent apertures called germ pores where sporopollenin is completely absent, allowing the emerging pollen tube to emerge during germination.

questions.question: Which of the following plants produces both chasmogamous (normal open) and cleistogamous (never-opening) flowers on the same individual?
questions.solution: Some plants such as Viola (common pansy), Oxalis, and Commelina produce two types of flowers: chasmogamous flowers (with exposed anthers and stigma) and cleistogamous flowers (which do not open at all).

questions.question: In water hyacinth (Eichhornia) and water lily (Nymphaea), pollination is carried out by:
options: Insects or Wind (because flowers emerge above water level)
questions.solution: In a majority of aquatic plants such as water hyacinth (Eichhornia crassipes) and water lily (Nymphaea), the flowers emerge above the level of water and are pollinated by insects or wind as in most land plants.

questions.question: Pollen-pistil interaction comprises a dynamic chemical dialogue involving:
options: Chemical recognition of compatible versus incompatible pollen by the pistil followed by promotion or inhibition of pollen tube growth
Only physical filtering based on pollen diameter
Electrical potential matching across the stigma
Immediate destruction of all pollen exines
questions.solution: Pollen-pistil interaction is a dynamic process involving pollen recognition mediated by chemical components of the pollen interacting with those of the pistil, allowing only compatible pollen to germinate and grow a pollen tube.

questions.question: During the early stages of embryogeny in dicotyledons, the zygote gives rise sequentially to:
options: Proembryo $\to$ Globular embryo $\to$ Heart-shaped embryo $\to$ Mature embryo
Heart-shaped embryo $\to$ Globular embryo $\to$ Proembryo $\to$ Mature embryo
Globular embryo $\to$ Proembryo $\to$ Torpedo embryo $\to$ Scutellum
Mature embryo $\to$ Globular embryo $\to$ Heart-shaped embryo
questions.solution: The zygote gives rise to the proembryo and subsequently to the globular, heart-shaped, and mature embryo (with two cotyledons and an embryonal axis).

questions.question:
Read the following statements regarding the morphological features of insect-pollinated flowers:
Statement I: Majority of insect-pollinated flowers are large, colorful, fragrant, and rich in nectar.
Statement II: Flowers pollinated by flies and beetles secrete foul odors to attract these animals.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.solution: Both statements are correct according to NCERT. Entomophilous flowers are large, showy, scented, and offer floral rewards (nectar and pollen). Flowers pollinated by dung flies and beetles emit foul odors to attract these specific pollinators.
